lines.en: What are your plans for the weekend?

lines.hz: 我早就想好了，打算跟朋友去饭馆吃饭，再去玩儿。
lines.py: Wǒ zǎojiù xiǎng hǎo le, dǎsuàn gēn péngyou qù fànguǎn chīfàn, zài qù wánr.
lines.en: I already figured it out long ago—I plan to eat at a restaurant with friends and then go hang out.

lines.hz: 你作业写完了吗？下个星期就要考试了。
lines.py: Nǐ zuòyè xiě wán le ma? Xià ge xīngqī jiù yào kǎoshì le.
lines.en: Have you finished your homework? There is an exam next week.

lines.hz: 别着急啊，我已经复习好了，现在什么都知道。
lines.py: Bié zháojí a, wǒ yǐjīng fùxí hǎo le, xiànzài shénme dōu zhīdào.
lines.en: Don't worry, I've already finished reviewing and know everything now.

texts.scene: At home — playing games too late
texts.title: 别一直玩儿游戏

lines.hz: 你从晚上七点一直玩儿电脑游戏到现在，怎么还不睡觉？
lines.py: Nǐ cóng wǎnshang qī diǎn yìzhí wánr diànnǎo yóuxì dào xiànzài, zěnme hái bú shuìjiào?
lines.en: You've been playing computer games straight from 7 PM until now—why aren't you sleeping yet?

lines.hz: 我觉得这个游戏很好玩儿，再玩儿一会儿就睡。
lines.py: Wǒ juéde zhège yóuxì hěn hǎowánr, zài wánr yíhuìr jiù shuì.
lines.en: I think this game is really fun; I'll sleep after playing a little longer.

lines.hz: 昨天医生说了，晚上不睡觉对人不好。
lines.py: Zuótiān yīshēng shuō le, wǎnshang bú shuìjiào duì rén bù hǎo.
lines.en: Yesterday the doctor said not sleeping at night is bad for you.

lines.hz: 好啊，那我先吃一点儿面包就去睡。
lines.py: Hǎo a, nà wǒ xiān chī yìdiǎnr miànbāo jiù qù shuì.
lines.en: Okay, then I'll eat a little bread first and go to sleep.

lines.hz: 下个月我要去北方旅游，正在准备东西。
lines.py: Xià ge yuè wǒ yào qù běifāng lǚyóu, zhèngzài zhǔnbèi dōngxi.
lines.en: Next month I'm traveling to the north, and I'm packing right now.

lines.hz: 北方比南方冷，但是宾馆里面不冷。你要带什么？
lines.py: Běifāng bǐ nánfāng lěng, dànshì bīnguǎn lǐmiàn bù lěng. Nǐ yào dài shénme?
lines.en: The north is colder than the south, but it's not cold inside the hotel. What are you taking?

lines.hz: 我打算带地图、一些衣服，还有几包方便面。
lines.py: Wǒ dǎsuàn dài dìtú, yìxiē yīfu, hái yǒu jǐ bāo fāngbiànmiàn.
lines.en: I plan to bring a map, some clothes, and a few packs of instant noodles.

lines.hz: 那边有很多饭馆，不要带那么多方便面。
lines.py: Nàbiān yǒu hěn duō fànguǎn, bú yào dài nàme duō fāngbiànmiàn.
lines.en: There are lots of restaurants over there—don't bring that many instant noodles.

lines.hz: 这个周末我要搬家，你能来帮我搬东西吗？
lines.py: Zhège zhōumò wǒ yào bānjiā, nǐ néng lái bāng wǒ bān dōngxi ma?
lines.en: I'm moving house this weekend—can you come help me move my things?

lines.hz: 没问题！你新家在哪儿？离宾馆远不远？
lines.py: Méi wèntí! Nǐ xīn jiā zài nǎr? Lí bīnguǎn yuǎn bù yuǎn?
lines.en: No problem! Where is your new place? Is it far from the hotel?

lines.hz: 不远，就在南方那个大公园旁边，走路十分钟就到。
lines.py: Bù yuǎn, jiù zài nánfāng nàge dà gōngyuán pángbiān, zǒulù shí fēnzhōng jiù dào.
lines.en: Not far, right next to that big park in the south—a ten-minute walk.

lines.hz: 太好了，搬完家我们一起去吃饭啊。
lines.py: Tài hǎo le, bān wán jiā wǒmen yìqǐ qù chīfàn a.
lines.en: Awesome, let's go grab a meal together after we finish moving.

grammar.title: Result complement 好 (completed & ready)
grammar.explain: Placed after a verb, 好 means the action is finished to a satisfactory, ready state—stronger than 完 (merely finished). Negative form uses 没 + V + 好.
grammar.pattern: S + V + 好 (+ O) + 了; negative: 没(有) + V + 好

examples.hz: 我已经复习好了。
examples.py: Wǒ yǐjīng fùxí hǎo le.
examples.en: I have already finished reviewing (and am ready).

examples.hz: 饭做好了，快来吃啊。
examples.py: Fàn zuò hǎo le, kuài lái chī a.
examples.en: Dinner is ready—come eat!

examples.hz: 周末打算我还没想好。
examples.py: Zhōumò dǎsuàn wǒ hái méi xiǎng hǎo.
examples.en: I haven't decided on my weekend plans yet.

grammar.point: 一 + M + 也/都 + 不/没
grammar.title: Emphatic negation (not even one / not at all)
grammar.explain: Combines 一 + measure word + noun with 也 or 都 and a negative verb to mean 'not even a single one'. With adjectives, 一点儿也/都不 means 'not at all'.
grammar.pattern: S + 一 + M (+ N) + 也/都 + 不/没 + V; S + 一点儿 + 也/都 + 不 + Adj

examples.hz: 我一点儿也不着急。
examples.py: Wǒ yìdiǎnr yě bù zháojí.
examples.en: I'm not worried at all.

examples.hz: 他一个面包都没吃。
examples.py: Tā yí ge miànbāo dōu méi chī.
examples.en: He didn't eat even a single piece of bread.

examples.hz: 我一杯咖啡也没喝。
examples.py: Wǒ yì bēi kāfēi yě méi hē.
examples.en: I didn't drink even one cup of coffee.

grammar.title: Conjunction 那 (well then / in that case)
grammar.explain: At the start of a sentence, 那 draws a natural conclusion or response based on what was just said—like 'well then' or 'in that case'.
grammar.pattern: [situation], 那 + [conclusion / decision]

examples.hz: 北方太冷了，那我们去南方啊。
examples.py: Běifāng tài lěng le, nà wǒmen qù nánfāng a.
examples.en: The north is too cold—then let's go to the south.

examples.hz: 你已经吃过饭了？那我就不做饭了。
examples.py: Nǐ yǐjīng chī guò fàn le? Nà wǒ jiù bú zuòfàn le.
examples.en: You already ate? Well then I won't cook.

examples.hz: 下雨了，那我们明天再搬家。
examples.py: Xiàyǔ le, nà wǒmen míngtiān zài bānjiā.
examples.en: It's raining—in that case let's move tomorrow.

grammar.title: 来/去 as simple direction complements
grammar.explain: After a verb, 来 means the movement comes toward the speaker and 去 means it goes away from the speaker. Common verbs are 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过 and 起, plus verbs like 拿, 带 and 买. A place object must go between the verb and 来/去 (回家去), while a thing object can go before or after 来/去.
grammar.pattern: V + 来/去; V + place + 来/去; V + thing + 来/去 or V + 来/去 + thing

examples.hz: 外边太冷了，快进来吧。
examples.py: Wàibian tài lěng le, kuài jìnlai ba.
examples.en: It's too cold outside, come on in.

examples.hz: 他昨天回中国去了。
examples.py: Tā zuótiān huí Zhōngguó qu le.
examples.en: He went back to China yesterday.

examples.hz: 我给你带来了一本书。
examples.py: Wǒ gěi nǐ dàilai le yì běn shū.
examples.en: I've brought you a book.

grammar.title: V1了 … 就 V2: as soon as one thing is done, the next follows
grammar.explain: Two actions happen one right after the other: the first, marked with 了, is completed, and 就 introduces the second, which starts straight away. It works for past events, habits and future plans. If the second action has its own subject, that subject goes right before 就.

examples.hz: 我每天回了家就洗澡。
examples.py: Wǒ měi tiān huíle jiā jiù xǐ zǎo.
examples.en: Every day I take a shower as soon as I get home.

examples.hz: 明天你到了机场就给我打电话。
examples.py: Míngtiān nǐ dàole jīchǎng jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.en: Call me as soon as you get to the airport tomorrow.

examples.hz: 老师来了我们就开始上课。
examples.py: Lǎoshī láile wǒmen jiù kāishǐ shàng kè.
examples.en: As soon as the teacher arrives, we'll start class.

grammar.title: 能……吗? as a rhetorical question
grammar.explain: Here 能……吗？ isn't a real question: the speaker already knows the answer and is making a point. The positive form means "no, it can't", and the negative form 能不……吗？ means "of course it will". It often comes after a reason, to criticise or to stress an obvious result.
grammar.pattern: 能 + V/Adj + 吗？ (= cannot); 能不 + V/Adj + 吗？ (= surely will)

examples.hz: 你天天不睡觉，身体能好吗？
examples.py: Nǐ tiāntiān bú shuì jiào, shēntǐ néng hǎo ma?
examples.en: You never get any sleep. How can you stay healthy?

examples.hz: 这么多作业，我一个晚上能写完吗？
examples.py: Zhème duō zuòyè, wǒ yí ge wǎnshang néng xiěwán ma?
examples.en: With this much homework, how could I finish it in one evening?

examples.hz: 他是你最好的朋友，他能不帮你吗？
examples.py: Tā shì nǐ zuì hǎo de péngyou, tā néng bù bāng nǐ ma?
examples.en: He's your best friend. Of course he'll help you.

grammar.title: 还是 vs 或者: "or" in questions and in statements
grammar.explain: Both mean "or". 还是 is used in questions that ask the listener to choose; 或者 is used in statements, meaning either option is fine. When a statement contains an embedded question, for example after 不知道 or 没想好, use 还是.
grammar.pattern: A 还是 B？; A 或者 B; 不知道 + A 还是 B

examples.hz: 你想坐公共汽车还是坐地铁？
examples.py: Nǐ xiǎng zuò gōnggòng qìchē háishi zuò dìtiě?
examples.en: Do you want to take the bus or the subway?

examples.hz: 周末我常常去公园或者去图书馆。
examples.py: Zhōumò wǒ chángcháng qù gōngyuán huòzhě qù túshūguǎn.
examples.en: On weekends I often go to the park or the library.

examples.hz: 我不知道他今天来还是明天来。
examples.py: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā jīntiān lái háishi míngtiān lái.
examples.en: I don't know whether he's coming today or tomorrow.

grammar.title: Location + V着 + noun: something is (placed) somewhere
grammar.explain: This pattern says what exists at a place and in what state: lying, written, sitting, living there and so on. The verb is typically 放, 写, 坐 or 住, and the noun is something unspecified (一本书, 几个人) rather than a particular "this book". In the negative, use 没 + V着 and drop the number and measure word.
grammar.pattern: Location + V着 + Num + MW + N; negative: Location + 没 + V着 + N

examples.hz: 门口站着两个人。
examples.py: Ménkǒu zhànzhe liǎng ge rén.
examples.en: Two people are standing at the door.

examples.hz: 黑板上写着几个汉字。
examples.py: Hēibǎn shang xiězhe jǐ ge Hànzì.
examples.en: A few Chinese characters are written on the blackboard.

examples.hz: 冰箱里没放着水果。
examples.py: Bīngxiāng li méi fàngzhe shuǐguǒ.
examples.en: There's no fruit in the fridge.

grammar.title: 会: will, be likely to (possibility)
grammar.explain: Besides "know how to", 会 can express a prediction: the speaker thinks something is likely to happen. It's mostly used about things that haven't happened yet, often with 的 at the end for a confident tone. The negative is 不会.
grammar.pattern: S + 会 + V/Adj (+ 的); negative: 不会

examples.hz: 明天会下雨吗？
examples.py: Míngtiān huì xià yǔ ma?
examples.en: Will it rain tomorrow?

examples.hz: 别担心，他不会忘记的。
examples.py: Bié dānxīn, tā bú huì wàngjì de.
examples.en: Don't worry, he won't forget.

examples.hz: 你这样每天练习，汉语水平一定会提高的。
examples.py: Nǐ zhèyàng měi tiān liànxí, Hànyǔ shuǐpíng yídìng huì tígāo de.
examples.en: If you practise like this every day, your Chinese will definitely improve.

grammar.title: 又 A 又 B: both A and B
grammar.explain: Says that a person or thing has two qualities at the same time. The two words are usually adjectives (sometimes verbs), and they normally point the same way, both good or both bad. Don't put 很 in front of the adjectives.
grammar.pattern: 又 + Adj1 + 又 + Adj2

examples.hz: 我的新房子又大又干净。
examples.py: Wǒ de xīn fángzi yòu dà yòu gānjìng.
examples.en: My new home is both big and clean.

examples.hz: 今天又刮风又下雨，我们别出去了。
examples.py: Jīntiān yòu guā fēng yòu xià yǔ, wǒmen bié chūqu le.
examples.en: It's windy and rainy today, so let's not go out.

examples.hz: 走了一天，我又累又饿。
examples.py: Zǒule yì tiān, wǒ yòu lèi yòu è.
examples.en: After walking all day, I'm tired and hungry.

grammar.title: V1着 + V2: doing one thing in a certain way or state
grammar.explain: Two actions happen at the same time, and the first one, marked with 着, describes the manner or state in which the second is done. V2 is the main action; V1着 tells you how, such as standing, sitting, smiling or holding something. For example, 走着去 means going on foot.

examples.hz: 我们走着去吧，不远。
examples.py: Wǒmen zǒuzhe qù ba, bù yuǎn.
examples.en: Let's walk there, it isn't far.

examples.hz: 孩子们笑着跑出去了。
examples.py: Háizimen xiàozhe pǎo chuqu le.
examples.en: The children ran out laughing.

examples.hz: 爸爸坐着看报纸，妈妈站着做饭。
examples.py: Bàba zuòzhe kàn bàozhǐ, māma zhànzhe zuò fàn.
examples.en: Dad reads the newspaper sitting down, and Mom cooks standing up.

grammar.title: Sentence-final 了: a change of situation
grammar.explain: At the end of a statement, 了 signals that things are now different from before or that a new situation has come about. It implies a contrast with the past: 我有工作了 means I didn't have one before and now I do. It works after adjectives, verbs, negatives and expressions of age or time.
grammar.pattern: S + … + 了

examples.hz: 天黑了，我们回家吧。
examples.py: Tiān hēi le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.en: It's getting dark, let's go home.

examples.hz: 我弟弟今年十八岁了。
examples.py: Wǒ dìdi jīnnián shíbā suì le.
examples.en: My younger brother is eighteen this year.

examples.hz: 他现在不喝咖啡了，只喝茶。
examples.py: Tā xiànzài bù hē kāfēi le, zhǐ hē chá.
examples.en: He doesn't drink coffee anymore, only tea.

grammar.title: 越来越: more and more
grammar.explain: Shows that a quality or feeling keeps growing as time goes on. It's followed directly by an adjective or a mental verb such as 喜欢 or 想. Degree adverbs like 很 or 非常 can't be added after it, and 了 often comes at the end.
grammar.pattern: S + 越来越 + Adj / mental V (+ 了)

examples.hz: 天气越来越热了。
examples.py: Tiānqì yuè lái yuè rè le.
examples.en: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.

examples.hz: 他的汉字写得越来越好。
examples.py: Tā de Hànzì xiě de yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.en: His Chinese characters are getting better and better.

examples.hz: 我越来越想我的家人了。
examples.py: Wǒ yuè lái yuè xiǎng wǒ de jiārén le.
examples.en: I miss my family more and more.

grammar.title: V得/不 + complement: can or can't manage to
grammar.explain: Put 得 or 不 between a verb and its complement to say whether the result can be reached: 听得懂 "can understand (what you hear)", 听不懂 "can't understand". The complement is usually a result word such as 完, 到, 懂 or 清楚, or a direction word such as 来 or 去. The 不 form is the normal way to say you can't manage something: 我看不清楚, not 我不能看清楚. To ask, add 吗 to the 得 form, or put the 得 and 不 forms side by side.
grammar.pattern: V + 得 + C (can); V + 不 + C (can't); question: V得C吗？ / V得C + V不C？

examples.hz: 黑板上的字太小了，我看不清楚。
examples.py: Hēibǎn shang de zì tài xiǎo le, wǒ kàn bu qīngchu.
examples.en: The writing on the board is too small. I can't make it out.

examples.hz: 他说的法语你听得懂吗？
examples.py: Tā shuō de Fǎyǔ nǐ tīng de dǒng ma?
examples.en: Can you understand the French he's speaking?

examples.hz: 我想了一个晚上，还是想不明白他为什么突然离开了。
examples.py: Wǒ xiǎngle yí ge wǎnshang, háishi xiǎng bu míngbai tā wèi shénme tūrán líkāi le.
examples.en: I thought about it all evening and still can't work out why he left so suddenly.

grammar.title: N + 呢？: asking where someone or something is
grammar.explain: A noun followed by 呢, with nothing else, asks where that person or thing is: 钥匙呢？ means "Where are the keys?" It's what you say when someone or something isn't where you expected, so it can sound surprised or impatient. Don't confuse it with 呢 after a statement, as in 我很好，你呢？, which asks "and what about you?"
grammar.pattern: N + 呢？ (= N 在哪儿？)

examples.hz: 妈妈，我的背包呢？
examples.py: Māma, wǒ de bēibāo ne?
examples.en: Mom, where's my backpack?

examples.hz: 小王呢？刚才他还在这儿。
examples.py: Xiǎo Wáng ne? Gāngcái tā hái zài zhèr.
examples.en: Where's Xiao Wang? He was here a minute ago.

examples.hz: 我放在桌子上的钢笔呢？谁拿走了？
examples.py: Wǒ fàng zài zhuōzi shang de gāngbǐ ne? Shéi názǒu le?
examples.en: Where's the pen I left on the desk? Who took it?

grammar.title: 刚 vs 刚才: just, just now
grammar.explain: Both say something happened a short time ago. 刚才 is a time word meaning "a few minutes ago": it can go before or after the subject, and it can describe a noun with 的 (刚才的电话). 刚 is an adverb that only goes right before the verb, and "a short time" is as the speaker sees it, so it can mean days or even months (我们刚认识三天). Sentences with 刚 usually don't end in 了, while 刚才 + a finished action usually does.
grammar.pattern: S + 刚 + V; 刚才 + S + V (+ 了) or S + 刚才 + V (+ 了); 刚才的 + N

examples.hz: 电影刚开始，你怎么就要走？
examples.py: Diànyǐng gāng kāishǐ, nǐ zěnme jiù yào zǒu?
examples.en: The film's only just started. Why are you leaving already?

examples.hz: 刚才给你打电话的是谁？
examples.py: Gāngcái gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà de shì shéi?
examples.en: Who was that on the phone just now?

examples.hz: 我们刚搬来半年，对这儿还不太了解。
examples.py: Wǒmen gāng bānlai bàn nián, duì zhèr hái bú tài liǎojiě.
examples.en: We only moved here six months ago, so we don't know the area well yet.

grammar.point: V + 了 + duration + O (+ 了)
grammar.title: Duration after the verb: how long something lasted, or has lasted so far
grammar.explain: To say how long an action lasts, put the length of time right after the verb and its 了; a noun object comes after the time: 打了两个小时篮球. A pronoun object comes before the time instead: 等了他半个小时. With just the one 了, the action lasted that long and is over; add another 了 at the end and it has gone on that long so far and is still going on.
grammar.pattern: S + V + 了 + duration + O; S + V + 了 + duration + O + 了 (still going on); V + 了 + pronoun + duration

examples.hz: 昨天晚上我睡了十个小时。
examples.py: Zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ shuìle shí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.en: I slept for ten hours last night.

examples.hz: 我们在公园打了一个半小时网球。
examples.py: Wǒmen zài gōngyuán dǎle yí ge bàn xiǎoshí wǎngqiú.
examples.en: We played tennis in the park for an hour and a half.

examples.hz: 你看了一个下午手机了，出去走走吧。
examples.py: Nǐ kànle yí ge xiàwǔ shǒujī le, chūqu zǒuzou ba.
examples.en: You've been on your phone all afternoon. Go out for a walk.

grammar.title: 对……感兴趣: to be interested in something
grammar.explain: To say what someone is interested in, put the topic after 对 and end with 感兴趣 or 有兴趣: 我对音乐感兴趣. 感兴趣 can't take an object directly, so 我感兴趣音乐 is wrong. Degree words go just before 感兴趣 or 有兴趣 (很感兴趣, 非常有兴趣), and the negatives are 不感兴趣 and 没(有)兴趣.
grammar.pattern: S + 对 + N/V + (很/不) 感兴趣; S + 对 + N/V + (很) 有兴趣 / 没(有)兴趣

examples.hz: 我妹妹对画画儿很感兴趣。
examples.py: Wǒ mèimei duì huà huàr hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.en: My little sister is really into drawing.

examples.hz: 我对做饭一点儿也不感兴趣，所以常常在外边吃。
examples.py: Wǒ duì zuò fàn yìdiǎnr yě bù gǎn xìngqù, suǒyǐ chángcháng zài wàibian chī.
examples.en: I'm not interested in cooking at all, so I often eat out.

examples.hz: 新来的同事对中国文化很有兴趣，常常问我问题。
examples.py: Xīn lái de tóngshì duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn yǒu xìngqù, chángcháng wèn wǒ wèntí.
examples.en: Our new colleague is very interested in Chinese culture and often asks me questions.

grammar.title: Telling the time with 半, 刻 and 差
grammar.explain: 半 after the hour means half past (三点半), and 刻 is a quarter of an hour, so 一刻 is a quarter past and 三刻 is a quarter to the next hour. 差 means "short of": 差 + minutes + the next hour gives the time just before it, as in 差十分六点 (5:50). For lengths of time, 一刻钟 is fifteen minutes and 半个小时 is half an hour; an hour and a half is 一个半小时.
grammar.pattern: hour + 点 + 半 / 一刻 / 三刻; 差 + minutes + hour + 点; 一刻钟, 半个小时, 一个半小时

examples.hz: 我们七点半在学校门口见吧。
examples.py: Wǒmen qī diǎn bàn zài xuéxiào ménkǒu jiàn ba.
examples.en: Let's meet at the school gate at seven thirty.

examples.hz: 现在差一刻九点，电影九点开始，我们得快点儿走。
examples.py: Xiànzài chà yí kè jiǔ diǎn, diànyǐng jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ, wǒmen děi kuài diǎnr zǒu.
examples.en: It's a quarter to nine and the film starts at nine, so we'd better hurry.

examples.hz: 他今天上班迟到了一刻钟，因为公共汽车八点一刻才来。
examples.py: Tā jīntiān shàng bān chídàole yí kè zhōng, yīnwèi gōnggòng qìchē bā diǎn yí kè cái lái.
examples.en: He was fifteen minutes late for work today because the bus didn't come until a quarter past eight.

grammar.title: 又 vs 再: "again" for repeats that have happened and repeats still to come
grammar.explain: Both mean "again" and go before the verb. 又 is for a repeat that has already happened, often with 了 and often with a note of surprise or annoyance (他又忘了). 再 is for a repeat that hasn't happened yet, so it shows up in plans, requests and suggestions (明天再来吧). One exception: 又 can also point ahead to a repeat that is bound to come, as in 明天又是星期一了.
grammar.pattern: 又 + V (+ 了): already repeated; 再 + V: will be repeated

examples.hz: 你说什么？我没听清楚，请再说一遍。
examples.py: Nǐ shuō shénme? Wǒ méi tīng qīngchu, qǐng zài shuō yí biàn.
examples.en: What did you say? I didn't catch that. Please say it again.

examples.hz: 他昨天忘了带钥匙，今天又忘了。
examples.py: Tā zuótiān wàngle dài yàoshi, jīntiān yòu wàng le.
examples.en: He forgot his keys yesterday, and today he forgot them again.

examples.hz: 你上个月刚换了手机，怎么又想换了？明年再换吧。
examples.py: Nǐ shàng ge yuè gāng huànle shǒujī, zěnme yòu xiǎng huàn le? Míngnián zài huàn ba.
examples.en: You only got a new phone last month. Why do you want another one already? Wait till next year.

grammar.title: The same question word twice, joined by 就: whoever, whatever, wherever
grammar.explain: Here the question words don't ask anything. The same question word appears in both halves, joined by 就, and both times it refers to the same person, thing, place or time, much like English "whoever", "whatever" or "wherever". The first half sets the condition and the second follows it: 你去哪儿我就去哪儿, "I'll go wherever you go". When the second half has its own subject, that subject comes before 就.
grammar.pattern: (S1) + V + QW, (S2) + 就 + V + QW

examples.hz: 你想吃什么就点什么，今天我请客。
examples.py: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme jiù diǎn shénme, jīntiān wǒ qǐng kè.
examples.en: Order whatever you like. It's my treat today.

examples.hz: 谁先到，谁就去买票。
examples.py: Shéi xiān dào, shéi jiù qù mǎi piào.
examples.en: Whoever gets there first goes and buys the tickets.

examples.hz: 周末你几点方便，我们就几点见面。
examples.py: Zhōumò nǐ jǐ diǎn fāngbiàn, wǒmen jiù jǐ diǎn jiàn miàn.
examples.en: This weekend we'll meet at whatever time suits you.

grammar.title: 越A越B: the more A, the more B
grammar.explain: This pattern ties two changes together: as A goes up, B goes up (or down) with it. With one subject it's often 越 + verb + 越 + adjective, as in 越走越快 "walk faster and faster". A and B can also be whole clauses with different subjects: 你越着急，他越慢. 越来越 (Lesson 5) is the fixed form for change over time, while 越A越B names what is driving the change.
grammar.pattern: S + 越 + V + 越 + Adj; 越 + A, (S) + 越 + B

examples.hz: 孩子们越玩儿越高兴。
examples.py: Háizimen yuè wánr yuè gāoxìng.
examples.en: The more the kids played, the happier they got.

examples.hz: 我们越走越远，最后找不到回家的路了。
examples.py: Wǒmen yuè zǒu yuè yuǎn, zuìhòu zhǎo bu dào huí jiā de lù le.
examples.en: We wandered further and further, and in the end we couldn't find our way home.

examples.hz: 你越不让他玩儿，他越想玩儿。
examples.py: Nǐ yuè bú ràng tā wánr, tā yuè xiǎng wánr.
examples.en: The more you stop him from playing, the more he wants to.

grammar.title: A跟B一样 (+ Adj): A is the same as B
grammar.explain: Use A跟B一样 to say two things come out the same when compared. 一样 on its own means "the same"; an adjective after it says in what way: 一样高 "just as tall". For "not the same", put 不 before 一样 (A跟B不一样), not before 跟. With a verb and 得, the comparison goes after 得: 他跑得跟我一样快.
grammar.pattern: A + 跟 + B + (不) 一样 (+ Adj); S + V得 + 跟 + B + 一样 + Adj

examples.hz: 我的手机跟你的一样。
examples.py: Wǒ de shǒujī gēn nǐ de yíyàng.
examples.en: My phone is the same as yours.

examples.hz: 我弟弟现在长得跟我一样高了。
examples.py: Wǒ dìdi xiànzài zhǎng de gēn wǒ yíyàng gāo le.
examples.en: My younger brother is as tall as me now.

examples.hz: 这儿的天气跟我们那儿很不一样，我还不太习惯。
examples.py: Zhèr de tiānqì gēn wǒmen nàr hěn bù yíyàng, wǒ hái bú tài xíguàn.
examples.en: The weather here is really different from back home. I'm still not used to it.

grammar.point: A比B + Adj + 一点儿/一些/得多/多了
grammar.title: 比 with 一点儿/得多/多了: a little or a lot more; A没有B: not as … as
grammar.explain: After the adjective in a 比 sentence you can say how big the gap is: 一点儿 or 一些 for a small difference, 得多 or 多了 for a big one. Don't use 很 or 非常 here; 我比他很高 is wrong. For "A is not as … as B", use A没有B + adjective, often with 这么 or 那么 before the adjective: 我没有他那么忙.
grammar.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adj + 一点儿/一些/得多/多了; negative: A + 没有 + B + (这么/那么) + Adj

examples.hz: 这件比那件便宜一点儿。
examples.py: Zhè jiàn bǐ nà jiàn piányi yìdiǎnr.
examples.en: This one's a bit cheaper than that one.

examples.hz: 坐地铁比坐公共汽车快得多。
examples.py: Zuò dìtiě bǐ zuò gōnggòng qìchē kuài de duō.
examples.en: Taking the subway is much faster than taking the bus.

examples.hz: 我个子没有哥哥那么高，但是跑得比他快多了。
examples.py: Wǒ gèzi méiyǒu gēge nàme gāo, dànshì pǎo de bǐ tā kuài duō le.
examples.en: I'm not as tall as my older brother, but I run a lot faster than he does.

grammar.title: Two neighbouring numbers for a rough amount: two or three, seven or eight
grammar.explain: Saying two neighbouring numbers together, smaller first, gives a rough figure: 两三天 "two or three days", 七八个人 "seven or eight people". There's no word for "or" between them, and the measure word follows as usual. It works with 一两 for "one or two" and above ten as well (十一二, 二三十), but not with 九十, which would just mean ninety.
grammar.pattern: n + (n+1) + MW + N: 一两个, 两三天, 七八个, 十一二个, 二三十个

examples.hz: 我每个星期打两三次篮球。
examples.py: Wǒ měi ge xīngqī dǎ liǎng sān cì lánqiú.
examples.en: I play basketball two or three times a week.

examples.hz: 你等我一两分钟，我马上就来。
examples.py: Nǐ děng wǒ yì liǎng fēnzhōng, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
examples.en: Give me a minute or two. I'll be right there.

examples.hz: 这次数学考试很难，我们班只有十一二个人考得不错。
examples.py: Zhè cì shùxué kǎoshì hěn nán, wǒmen bān zhǐ yǒu shíyī èr ge rén kǎo de búcuò.
examples.en: This maths test was hard. Only eleven or twelve people in our class did well.

grammar.title: 把 sentences (1): doing something to a specific thing
grammar.explain: A 把 B + V moves the object B in front of the verb to focus on what A does to it, and it's typical of requests, orders and reminders. B has to be something specific that both speakers know about, and the verb can't end the sentence bare: here it's followed by 了, meaning the thing gets dealt with (washed, returned, forgotten). Negatives such as 没 and 别 and modal verbs such as 能 and 可以 go in front of 把, not in front of the verb.
grammar.pattern: A + 把 + B + V + 了; 没/别/不/能/可以 + 把 + B + V + 了

examples.hz: 吃完饭，你把筷子洗了吧。
examples.py: Chīwán fàn, nǐ bǎ kuàizi xǐ le ba.
examples.en: When we've finished eating, could you wash the chopsticks?

examples.hz: 我把图书馆的书还了，现在可以再借几本了。
examples.py: Wǒ bǎ túshūguǎn de shū huán le, xiànzài kěyǐ zài jiè jǐ běn le.
examples.en: I've returned the library books, so now I can borrow a few more.

examples.hz: 明天的会议很重要，你别把这件事忘了。
examples.py: Míngtiān de huìyì hěn zhòngyào, nǐ bié bǎ zhè jiàn shì wàng le.
examples.en: Tomorrow's meeting is important, so don't forget about it.

grammar.title: Number + 左右: about, or so
grammar.explain: Put 左右 after a number to show it's only a rough figure: "about" or "or so". It goes after the whole number phrase, including the measure word or unit, so you say 十分钟左右 or 五块钱左右. It works for clock times, prices, ages, amounts and lengths of time.
grammar.pattern: Num (+ MW/unit) (+ N) + 左右

examples.hz: 这儿一瓶啤酒五块钱左右。
examples.py: Zhèr yì píng píjiǔ wǔ kuài qián zuǒyòu.
examples.en: A bottle of beer here costs about five yuan.

examples.hz: 从我家走到图书馆要十分钟左右。
examples.py: Cóng wǒ jiā zǒudào túshūguǎn yào shí fēnzhōng zuǒyòu.
examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to walk from my place to the library.

examples.hz: 会议下午三点开始，五点左右结束。
examples.py: Huìyì xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ, wǔ diǎn zuǒyòu jiéshù.
examples.en: The meeting starts at 3 p.m. and finishes around 5.

grammar.title: 就 vs 才: sooner than expected vs later than expected
grammar.explain: 就 and 才 both sit right before the verb and show how the speaker feels about a time or an amount. 就 means it happened early, fast or easily ("already", "only took"), and the sentence often ends with 了. 才 means it happened late, slowly or with trouble ("not until", "only then"), and usually has no 了 after the verb. The same fact can be told either way: 他七点就来了 sounds early, while 他七点才来 sounds late.
grammar.pattern: time/amount + 就 + V (+ 了); time/amount + 才 + V

examples.hz: 电影七点开始，他六点半就到了。
examples.py: Diànyǐng qī diǎn kāishǐ, tā liù diǎn bàn jiù dào le.
examples.en: The film started at seven, and he was already there at six thirty.

examples.hz: 我等了他一个小时，他十点才来。
examples.py: Wǒ děngle tā yí ge xiǎoshí, tā shí diǎn cái lái.
examples.en: I waited an hour for him, and he didn't show up until ten.

examples.hz: 这本书我两天就看完了，我弟弟看了两个星期才看完。
examples.py: Zhè běn shū wǒ liǎng tiān jiù kànwán le, wǒ dìdi kànle liǎng ge xīngqī cái kànwán.
examples.en: I finished this book in just two days, but it took my younger brother two weeks.

grammar.title: 把 sentences (2): putting something somewhere or giving it to someone
grammar.explain: When an action moves a specific thing to a place, use 把 + thing + V + 在/到 + place, as in 把书放在桌子上. When the action hands the thing over to someone, use 把 + thing + V + 给 + person, as in 把钱还给他. The place or person has to follow the verb directly, so the thing can't go there too, and 把 brings it in front of the verb. As before, 没, 别 and modal verbs go before 把.
grammar.pattern: A + 把 + B + V + 在/到 + place; A + 把 + B + V + 给 + person

examples.hz: 请把你的名字写在黑板上。
examples.py: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de míngzi xiě zài hēibǎn shang.
examples.en: Please write your name on the blackboard.

examples.hz: 我已经把护照放到包里了，不会忘的。
examples.py: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ hùzhào fàngdào bāo li le, bú huì wàng de.
examples.en: I've already put my passport in my bag, so I won't forget it.

examples.hz: 要是你需要，我可以把我的自行车借给你。
examples.py: Yàoshi nǐ xūyào, wǒ kěyǐ bǎ wǒ de zìxíngchē jiè gěi nǐ.
examples.en: If you need it, I can lend you my bike.

grammar.point: V + 上/下/进/出/回/过/起 + 来/去
grammar.title: Compound direction complements: 进来, 出去, 回来, 起来 …
grammar.explain: After a verb you can add two direction words: first one for the path (上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过, 起), then 来 for movement toward the speaker or 去 for movement away, as in 跑出去 or 站起来 (起 only takes 来). If the object is a place, it has to go between the two parts: 跑回家去. If it's an ordinary thing, it can go between them or after the whole complement (拿出两个苹果来 / 拿出来两个苹果), and when the action is already done it usually comes last.
grammar.pattern: V + 上/下/进/出/回/过/起 + 来/去; V + 进/出/回/上/下 + place + 来/去; V + 出/回… + thing + 来/去 or V + 出来/回来… + thing

examples.hz: 校长来了，大家都站起来了。
examples.py: Xiàozhǎng lái le, dàjiā dōu zhàn qilai le.
examples.en: The principal came in, and everyone stood up.

examples.hz: 爷爷慢慢地走回房间去了。
examples.py: Yéye mànmàn de zǒuhuí fángjiān qu le.
examples.en: Grandpa slowly walked back to his room.

examples.hz: 奶奶从包里拿出来一件礼物送给我。
examples.py: Nǎinai cóng bāo li ná chulai yí jiàn lǐwù sòng gěi wǒ.
examples.en: Grandma took a present out of her bag and gave it to me.

grammar.title: 一边 … 一边 …: doing two things at once
grammar.explain: Put 一边 in front of each of two verb phrases to show one person doing both at the same time. The subject is said once, at the start. In short phrases the 一 is often dropped, as in 边走边说. Both parts should be actions you actively do, not states or feelings.
grammar.pattern: S + 一边 + V1 (+ O1) + 一边 + V2 (+ O2); S + 边 + V1 + 边 + V2

examples.hz: 我经常一边听音乐一边跑步。
examples.py: Wǒ jīngcháng yìbiān tīng yīnyuè yìbiān pǎo bù.
examples.en: I often listen to music while I run.

examples.hz: 别一边吃饭一边看手机。
examples.py: Bié yìbiān chī fàn yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
examples.en: Don't look at your phone while you're eating.

examples.hz: 我们边走边聊，没想到一会儿就到了。
examples.py: Wǒmen biān zǒu biān liáo, méi xiǎngdào yíhuìr jiù dào le.
examples.en: We chatted as we walked, and before we knew it we were there.

grammar.title: 把 sentences (3): 把 with a result or direction complement
grammar.explain: A very common 把 sentence puts a complement after the verb to say what happens to B. A result complement shows the state B ends up in (洗干净, 做好, 吃完), and a direction complement shows where B moves (拿出来, 放进去). B is again something specific, and to say it hasn't happened yet, put 没 or 还没 before 把.
grammar.pattern: A + 把 + B + V + result complement (+ 了); A + 把 + B + V + direction complement; 没 + 把 + B + V + complement

examples.hz: 我已经把盘子洗干净了。
examples.py: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ pánzi xǐ gānjìng le.
examples.en: I've already washed the plates.

examples.hz: 外面刮风了，快把衣服拿进来吧。
examples.py: Wàimian guā fēng le, kuài bǎ yīfu ná jinlai ba.
examples.en: The wind's picking up outside. Quick, bring the laundry in.

examples.hz: 叔叔把桌子上的香蕉都吃完了，一个也没给我留。
examples.py: Shūshu bǎ zhuōzi shang de xiāngjiāo dōu chīwán le, yí ge yě méi gěi wǒ liú.
examples.en: My uncle ate all the bananas on the table and didn't leave a single one for me.

grammar.title: 先 …, 再/又 …, 然后 …: first, next, then
grammar.explain: This frame lists actions in the order they happen. 先 marks the first step and 然后 a later one, and 再 or 又 can add a step in between. Use 再 for steps that are still to come, such as plans and instructions, and 又 for steps that already happened, usually with 了. 然后 is often followed by 再 when the step is still in the future.
grammar.pattern: 先 + V1, 再 + V2, 然后 + V3 (not done yet); 先 + V1了, 又 + V2了, 然后 + V3 (already done)

examples.hz: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影吧。
examples.py: Wǒmen xiān chī fàn, ránhòu qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.en: Let's eat first and then go see a movie.

examples.hz: 你先洗个澡，再吃点儿东西，然后早点儿睡觉。
examples.py: Nǐ xiān xǐ ge zǎo, zài chī diǎnr dōngxi, ránhòu zǎo diǎnr shuì jiào.
examples.en: Take a shower first, then have something to eat, and after that get to bed early.

examples.hz: 昨天我先打扫了房间，又洗了衣服，然后去超市买了点儿菜。
examples.py: Zuótiān wǒ xiān dǎsǎole fángjiān, yòu xǐle yīfu, ránhòu qù chāoshì mǎile diǎnr cài.
examples.en: Yesterday I cleaned my room first, then did the laundry, and after that went to the supermarket to buy some groceries.

grammar.title: 除了 … (以外): except, or besides
grammar.explain: 除了 X (以外) sets X aside, and the second half says what holds for the rest. With 都, X is the exception: 除了他，我们都去了 means all of us went except him. With 还 or 也, X counts too and something more is added: "besides X, also …". 以外 can be left out, and the subject goes either at the very start or just before 都/还/也.
grammar.pattern: 除了 + X (+ 以外)，(S +) 都 + … (except); 除了 + X (+ 以外)，(S +) 还/也 + … (besides)

examples.hz: 除了星期天，我每天都上班。
examples.py: Chúle xīngqītiān, wǒ měi tiān dōu shàng bān.
examples.en: I work every day except Sunday.

examples.hz: 除了水果以外，我还买了一些牛奶和面包。
examples.py: Chúle shuǐguǒ yǐwài, wǒ hái mǎile yìxiē niúnǎi hé miànbāo.
examples.en: Besides fruit, I also bought some milk and bread.

examples.hz: 除了上课以外，留学生们也经常参加一些中国文化活动。
examples.py: Chúle shàng kè yǐwài, liúxuéshēngmen yě jīngcháng cānjiā yìxiē Zhōngguó wénhuà huódòng.
examples.en: Besides going to class, the international students also often take part in Chinese cultural events.

grammar.title: 什么 meaning "any" or "anything"
grammar.explain: 什么 doesn't always ask "what". In a yes-no question (有没有什么……？ or ……什么……吗？), after 没 or 不, or in an "if" sentence, it stands for something unspecified: "any" or "anything". It makes the sentence softer and more polite, and taking it out barely changes the meaning: 没什么事 and 没事 both mean "nothing's up".
grammar.pattern: 有没有 + 什么 + N？; V + 什么 + 吗？; 没(有) + 什么 + N

examples.hz: 你想喝点儿什么吗？
examples.py: Nǐ xiǎng hē diǎnr shénme ma?
examples.en: Would you like something to drink?

examples.hz: 今天没什么重要的新闻。
examples.py: Jīntiān méi shénme zhòngyào de xīnwén.
examples.en: There isn't any important news today.

examples.hz: 去中国留学以前，你有没有什么要准备的？
examples.py: Qù Zhōngguó liú xué yǐqián, nǐ yǒu méiyǒu shénme yào zhǔnbèi de?
examples.en: Is there anything you need to get ready before you go to study in China?

grammar.title: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
grammar.explain: Put 极了 right after an adjective or a feeling verb such as 喜欢, 担心 or 满意 to say it's at the highest degree: "extremely" or "incredibly". Don't add 很 or 非常 in front, and don't put an object after it; move the object to the front of the sentence instead. It's lively and spoken, good for strong reactions.
grammar.pattern: Adj / mental V + 极了

examples.hz: 这个西瓜甜极了。
examples.py: Zhège xīguā tián jíle.
examples.en: This watermelon is incredibly sweet.

examples.hz: 听到这个新闻，大家都高兴极了。
examples.py: Tīngdào zhège xīnwén, dàjiā dōu gāoxìng jíle.
examples.en: Everyone was thrilled to hear the news.

examples.hz: 孩子到晚上十点还没回家，妈妈担心极了。
examples.py: Háizi dào wǎnshang shí diǎn hái méi huí jiā, māma dānxīn jíle.
examples.en: It was ten at night and the child still wasn't home, so Mom was worried sick.

grammar.title: 如果 … (的话), 就 …: if …, then …
grammar.explain: 如果 sets up a condition that may or may not come true, and the clause with 就 says what follows if it does. You can add 的话 at the end of the condition, and in casual speech 如果 is sometimes dropped, leaving just ……的话. If the second clause has its own subject, that subject goes in front of 就, never after it.
grammar.pattern: 如果 + condition (+ 的话), (S) + 就 + result

examples.hz: 如果你饿了，就先吃吧，不用等我。
examples.py: Rúguǒ nǐ è le, jiù xiān chī ba, búyòng děng wǒ.
examples.en: If you're hungry, go ahead and eat. Don't wait for me.

examples.hz: 如果周末天气好的话，我们就去公园走走。
examples.py: Rúguǒ zhōumò tiānqì hǎo dehuà, wǒmen jiù qù gōngyuán zǒuzou.
examples.en: If the weather's nice this weekend, we'll go for a walk in the park.

examples.hz: 如果这双皮鞋穿着不舒服，你就拿回来换一双。
examples.py: Rúguǒ zhè shuāng píxié chuānzhe bù shūfu, nǐ jiù ná huilai huàn yì shuāng.
examples.en: If these leather shoes aren't comfortable, just bring them back and swap them for another pair.

grammar.title: Complex complement of state: so … that …
grammar.explain: The complement after 得 doesn't have to be a single word like 很好; it can be a whole verb phrase or even a short clause with its own subject. That phrase shows how far a feeling or state goes, usually by saying what it makes someone do or unable to do, much like English "so … that …". The word before 得 is usually an adjective or a verb of feeling, such as 累, 忙, 冷, 高兴 or 想.
grammar.pattern: S + Adj/V + 得 + verb phrase / clause

examples.hz: 我忙得忘了吃午饭。
examples.py: Wǒ máng de wàngle chī wǔfàn.
examples.en: I was so busy I forgot to have lunch.

examples.hz: 女儿考了一百分，高兴得在房间里跑来跑去。
examples.py: Nǚ'ér kǎole yìbǎi fēn, gāoxìng de zài fángjiān li pǎo lái pǎo qù.
examples.en: My daughter got full marks and was so happy she ran all around her room.

examples.hz: 这个城市的冬天冷得大家都不想出门。
examples.py: Zhège chéngshì de dōngtiān lěng de dàjiā dōu bù xiǎng chū mén.
examples.en: Winters in this city are so cold that nobody wants to leave the house.

grammar.title: AA的: doubling a one-syllable adjective for a vivid description
grammar.explain: Doubling a one-syllable adjective (红 → 红红的, 长 → 长长的) makes a description more vivid and suggests a high degree, often with a warm, affectionate feel. The doubled form normally takes 的 and paints what a person or thing looks or feels like, either after the noun or in front of it. Because the doubling already adds emphasis, don't put 很 or 非常 in front of it, and don't negate it with 不.
grammar.pattern: N + AA的; AA的 + N

examples.hz: 她的声音甜甜的，大家都喜欢听她唱歌。
examples.py: Tā de shēngyīn tiántián de, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tīng tā chàng gē.
examples.en: She has such a sweet voice that everyone loves hearing her sing.

examples.hz: 他个子高高的，头发短短的，穿着一双黑皮鞋。
examples.py: Tā gèzi gāogāo de, tóufa duǎnduǎn de, chuānzhe yì shuāng hēi píxié.
examples.en: He's tall with short hair, and he's wearing black leather shoes.

examples.hz: 今天外边太冷了，我想喝一杯热热的茶。
examples.py: Jīntiān wàibian tài lěng le, wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi rèrè de chá.
examples.en: It's freezing out today. I could really use a nice hot cup of tea.

grammar.title: ABAB: doubling a two-syllable verb for "a bit" or "have a go"
grammar.explain: A two-syllable verb is doubled as a whole word, ABAB (休息休息, never 休休息息), to show that an action is short, relaxed or just a try. Like adding 一下, it makes suggestions and requests sound lighter and friendlier. Only actions someone chooses to do are doubled this way, so verbs like 喜欢 or 认为 aren't. Verb-object words such as 聊天 double only the verb part: 聊聊天.
grammar.pattern: AB + AB (+ O); verb-object words: A + A + B

examples.hz: 我们休息休息再走吧。
examples.py: Wǒmen xiūxi xiūxi zài zǒu ba.
examples.en: Let's rest a little before we carry on.

examples.hz: 你要见他爸爸妈妈？那你得好好儿准备准备。
examples.py: Nǐ yào jiàn tā bàba māma? Nà nǐ děi hǎohāor zhǔnbèi zhǔnbèi.
examples.en: You're meeting his parents? Then you'd better get properly prepared.

examples.hz: 我刚来这个城市，想先了解了解这儿的生活。
examples.py: Wǒ gāng lái zhège chéngshì, xiǎng xiān liǎojiě liǎojiě zhèr de shēnghuó.
examples.en: I've only just moved to this city, so first I'd like to get a feel for life here.

grammar.point: 谁/什么/哪儿/怎么 + 都/也
grammar.title: Question words + 都/也: everyone, everything, everywhere, any way
grammar.explain: A question word doesn't always ask a question. Followed by 都 or 也, it covers every member of a group with no exceptions: 谁都 "everyone", 什么都 "everything", 哪儿都 "everywhere", 怎么都 "in any way", 什么时候都 "at any time". The question word comes before 都/也 and the verb. With a negative it means "no one", "nothing" or "nowhere": 他什么也没说 means he said nothing at all.
grammar.pattern: 谁/什么/哪儿/怎么/什么时候 + 都/也 + V; negative: … + 都/也 + 不/没 + V

examples.hz: 这个问题太简单了，谁都会回答。
examples.py: Zhège wèntí tài jiǎndān le, shéi dōu huì huídá.
examples.en: This question is so easy that anyone could answer it.

examples.hz: 我已经吃饱了，什么也不想吃了。
examples.py: Wǒ yǐjīng chībǎo le, shénme yě bù xiǎng chī le.
examples.en: I'm already full. I don't want anything else to eat.

examples.hz: 放假的时候我哪儿也没去，一直在家休息。
examples.py: Fàng jià de shíhou wǒ nǎr yě méi qù, yìzhí zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.en: I didn't go anywhere over the holidays. I just stayed home and rested.

grammar.title: 只要 …, 就 …: as long as …
grammar.explain: 只要 names a condition that is enough on its own: once it's met, the result after 就 follows. It often sounds encouraging, as if the condition isn't hard to meet. The subject can go before or after 只要, and if the result has a different subject, that subject goes right before 就.
grammar.pattern: (S) + 只要 + condition, (S2) + 就 + result

examples.hz: 只要有机会，我就去别的国家旅游。
examples.py: Zhǐyào yǒu jīhuì, wǒ jiù qù biéde guójiā lǚyóu.
examples.en: Whenever I get the chance, I go travelling abroad.

examples.hz: 只要每天练习，你的汉语就会越来越好。
examples.py: Zhǐyào měi tiān liànxí, nǐ de Hànyǔ jiù huì yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.en: As long as you practise every day, your Chinese will keep getting better.

examples.hz: 你只要向前走五分钟，就能看到那家银行。
examples.py: Nǐ zhǐyào xiàng qián zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng, jiù néng kàndào nà jiā yínháng.
examples.en: Just walk straight ahead for five minutes and you'll see the bank.

grammar.title: 关于: about, on (a topic)
grammar.explain: 关于 + a noun phrase marks what something is about. It can describe a noun with 的 (关于历史的书, books about history), or open a sentence to set its topic (关于这件事, …). When it sets the topic of the whole sentence, it goes before the subject, not after it.
grammar.pattern: 关于 + N + 的 + N; 关于 + N, S + V …

examples.hz: 我很喜欢看关于动物的书。
examples.py: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan kàn guānyú dòngwù de shū.
examples.en: I love reading books about animals.

examples.hz: 关于明天的考试，老师说了几个要注意的地方。
examples.py: Guānyú míngtiān de kǎoshì, lǎoshī shuōle jǐ ge yào zhùyì de dìfang.
examples.en: About tomorrow's exam, the teacher mentioned a few things to watch out for.

examples.hz: 关于这个城市的历史，他知道得比谁都多。
examples.py: Guānyú zhège chéngshì de lìshǐ, tā zhīdào de bǐ shéi dōu duō.
examples.en: When it comes to this city's history, he knows more than anyone.

grammar.point: V + 出来 / 下来 / 起来; 看上去
grammar.title: Extended meanings of directional complements: 出来, 下来, 起来, 看上去
grammar.explain: Directional complements don't only describe movement. V + 出来 can mean something new is produced (想出来, come up with) or something hidden is recognised (看出来, 听出来, tell or make out). After an adjective or verb, 下来 shows things settling: from moving to still, noisy to quiet, fast to slow (停下来, 安静下来), while 想/记 + 起来 means a memory comes back. 看上去 and 看起来 mean "look" or "seem", a judgement based on appearance.
grammar.pattern: V + 出来 (create / recognise); Adj/V + 下来 (settle down); 想/记 + 起来 (recall); 看上去 / 看起来 + description

examples.hz: 我突然想起来，今天是妈妈的生日！
examples.py: Wǒ tūrán xiǎng qilai, jīntiān shì māma de shēngrì!
examples.en: It suddenly hit me: today is Mom's birthday!

examples.hz: 晚上十点以后，街上慢慢安静下来了。
examples.py: Wǎnshang shí diǎn yǐhòu, jiē shang mànmàn ānjìng xialai le.
examples.en: After ten at night, the streets gradually went quiet.

examples.hz: 这两张照片看上去差不多，你能看出来哪张是今年照的吗？
examples.py: Zhè liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn kàn shangqu chàbuduō, nǐ néng kàn chulai nǎ zhāng shì jīnnián zhào de ma?
examples.en: These two photos look almost the same. Can you tell which one was taken this year?

grammar.title: 使 / 叫 / 让: to make someone feel or do something
grammar.explain: 使, 叫 and 让 can all mean "make" or "cause": in A + 使/叫/让 + B + verb or adjective, A causes B to feel or do something. B is the object of 使/叫/让 and at the same time the subject of what follows. The meaning is basically the same; 使 belongs to written Chinese, 叫 to casual speech, and 让 fits both. A is very often an event or a thing rather than a person.
grammar.pattern: A + 使/叫/让 + B + V/Adj

examples.hz: 他的话让我很难过。
examples.py: Tā de huà ràng wǒ hěn nánguò.
examples.en: What he said really upset me.

examples.hz: 你怎么才回来？叫我们等了这么久。
examples.py: Nǐ zěnme cái huílai? Jiào wǒmen děngle zhème jiǔ.
examples.en: Why are you only back now? You kept us waiting so long.

examples.hz: 这次比赛使大家的关系变得更好了。
examples.py: Zhè cì bǐsài shǐ dàjiā de guānxì biàn de gèng hǎo le.
examples.en: The competition brought everyone closer together.

grammar.title: 被 sentences: the passive
grammar.explain: In a 被 sentence the subject is the one something happens to, and the doer comes after 被: S + 被 + doer + verb + something more. The verb can't stand alone; it is followed by 了, a complement or a place phrase. The doer after 被 may be left out, but after the colloquial 叫 or 让 it must be there. Negatives and modal verbs such as 没, 不, 会 and 能 go before 被, and the pattern often describes something unwelcome.
grammar.pattern: S + 被/叫/让 + (doer) + V + other; S + 没/会/能 + 被 + (doer) + V + other

examples.hz: 我的名字被老师写错了。
examples.py: Wǒ de míngzi bèi lǎoshī xiěcuò le.
examples.en: The teacher wrote my name wrong.

examples.hz: 桌子上的那碗米饭让小狗吃了。
examples.py: Zhuōzi shang de nà wǎn mǐfàn ràng xiǎo gǒu chī le.
examples.en: The dog ate the bowl of rice that was on the table.

examples.hz: 别把钱放在这儿，会被别人拿走的。
examples.py: Bié bǎ qián fàng zài zhèr, huì bèi biérén názǒu de.
examples.en: Don't leave your money here. Someone might take it.

grammar.title: 只有 …, 才 …: only if …
grammar.explain: 只有 introduces the one condition without which the result can't happen, and the result is marked by 才, not 就. It's stricter than 只要……就……: 只要 says a condition is enough, while 只有 says it's the only way. 只有 can also go right before a person or thing (只有他才知道, only he knows), and if the result has its own subject, it goes in front of 才.
grammar.pattern: 只有 + condition, (S) + 才 + result; 只有 + N + 才 + V

examples.hz: 只有多听多说，才能学好汉语。
examples.py: Zhǐyǒu duō tīng duō shuō, cái néng xuéhǎo Hànyǔ.
examples.en: Only by listening and speaking a lot can you learn Chinese well.

examples.hz: 这个问题只有王老师才能解决。
examples.py: Zhège wèntí zhǐyǒu Wáng lǎoshī cái néng jiějué.
examples.en: Only Teacher Wang can solve this problem.

examples.hz: 只有你相信自己，别人才会相信你。
examples.py: Zhǐyǒu nǐ xiāngxìn zìjǐ, biérén cái huì xiāngxìn nǐ.
examples.en: Only when you believe in yourself will other people believe in you.
